population.span: Hospitalized patients were eligible for the trial if they had clinically suspected or laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and no medical history that might, in the opinion of the attending clinician, put patients at substantial risk if they were to participate in the trial.

endpoint.span: The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within 28 days after randomization; further analyses were specified at 6 months.

estimate.span: Overall, 482 patients (22.9%) in the dexamethasone group and 1110 patients (25.7%) in the usual care group died within 28 days after randomization (age-adjusted rate ratio, 0.83; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.75 to 0.93; P<0.001).

ci.span: Overall, 482 patients (22.9%) in the dexamethasone group and 1110 patients (25.7%) in the usual care group died within 28 days after randomization (age-adjusted rate ratio, 0.83; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.75 to 0.93; P<0.001).

analysis_set.span: All analyses were performed according to the intention-to-treat principle.

treatment_strategy.span: Eligible and consenting patients were assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive either the usual standard of care alone or the usual standard of care plus oral or intravenous dexamethasone (at a dose of 6 mg once daily) for up to 10 days (or until hospital discharge if sooner)

follow_up.span: The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within 28 days after randomization; further analyses were specified at 6 months.

served_mismatch: The served estimate and confidence limits match the overall intention-to-treat 28-day mortality result. However, the source reports an age-adjusted mortality rate ratio estimated using a Cox hazard ratio, not a risk ratio or the OR specified in served_outcome.estimand.

candidate_rejections.span: For the primary outcome of 28-day mortality, the hazard ratio from Cox regression was used to estimate the mortality rate ratio.
candidate_rejections.why: Reject interpreting the served RR candidate as a risk ratio or odds ratio; retain the reported numbers as a Cox hazard ratio described by the authors as a mortality rate ratio.

entry_population_matches_question.why: Entry included hospitalized patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19, but eligibility was broadened beyond adults; the reported analysis follows intention-to-treat.
entry_population_matches_question.span: Initially, recruitment was limited to patients who were at least 18 years of age, but the age limit was removed starting on May 9, 2020.

notes: All spans are from the held full text. HR denotes the stated Cox estimator; the publication calls the effect an age-adjusted rate ratio. No odds ratio was calculated. The age-eligibility statement does not establish that children were actually randomized in this comparison.
